It lists what `habeas mdbook` reads and what it does not do: audit, check freshness, enforce coverage, load measurements, run tests, or invoke a model. It also says read and parse failures become rendering diagnostics rather than a validation verdict. None of these clauses names a library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or interface that the implementation must delegate through. I considered an alternative built differently, such as different module structure or a different parser. If it renders the same output from the same inputs and performs none of the prohibited reads or checks, it still satisfies the text. The how-it-is-built choices are therefore discretionary. The obligations are input and output behavior constraints. They are not structural constraints, so no implementation root is needed and none is supplied. Whether rendering avoids the prohibited inputs is a behavioral question for the test criterion. behavioral: The subject has three behavioral obligations. It also requires that coverage documentation be rendered from source annotations and stored reviews. The cited `requirements.index.render_only` is context here. 1. **Saved execution measurements are not read.** - `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[book_ignores_saved_measurements_and_preserves_artifacts]` creates a saved attempt with `record(...)`, using the test name `saved-test-name-should-never-appear`. - It asserts that the rendered chapters are identical to the render made with no saved data. - It asserts that the test name never appears, that there is no `Missing`, `Recorded true`, `Recorded false`, `Recorded FIXME`, or `Unreadable`. - It asserts that no acceptance wording such as "current and accepted" appears. - The overview omits "0 unresolved gaps", so no computed acceptance or resolution verdict is shown. - The unreadable and invalid cases cover the readable-diagnostic part of the cited requirement. 3. **Review freshness is not audited.** - The same test stores a review with the hash `old hash`, or no hash at all. It then edits the source so the review would be stale. - It asserts that the rendered output still shows the stored review and its rationale, with no "input is stale" text. - It asserts that the review file bytes are unchanged. - It checks that the justification shown is the current one from the source, both when it is updated and when it is removed. - This covers rendering from source annotations plus stored reviews. 4. **The cited `requirements.index.render_only` is applied in the subject's case.** `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[book_rendering_preserves_retained_coverage_and_never_launches_tests]` renders the coverage index and checks that only `cargo metadata` calls are made. The other two tests also carry `{test}` markers for the subject. I found no unmarked relevant tests and no untested obligation. The assertions enforce the expected outcomes.
